statements.text: I think we all agree. Medicare was built on a simple promise that after a lifetime of work Americans should be able to get the healthcare they have earned. [...] And prior authorization by artificial intelligence is putting the judgement of doctors and the needs of patients behind.
statements.venue: House Appropriations Committee markup remarks, reported by Healthcare Dive

statements.text: AI needs to be a tool for the doctor. A doctor should not be a tool for AI, nor should AI be allowed to be used as a weapon to deny care. and that's what we're worried about now,
statements.venue: Press conference on Medicare WISeR AI prior authorization pilot, reported by WPBF

statements.text:
This week, I was proud to announce $1.031 million for a new AI & Cybersecurity Training Center at @PBStateCollege.

This investment will help equip students with in-demand skills, strengthen our workforce, and position Palm Beach County as a leader in innovation. https://t.co/c5Mhhc01Rt

When a doctor says a patient needs care, that should be the end of the story.

Instead, Medicare launched a pilot program that lets private companies use AI to second-guess physicians and delay treatment.

I’m proud my amendment to halt further funding for this scheme was included in the FY27 LHHS funding bill. 

Seniors earned their benefits. They deserve care, not bureaucratic obstacles.
No community should be forced to have a data center if it's going to have a serious impact on its environmental footprint.
statements.venue: WLRN interview on AI data center (Project Tango)
